name: Cobra Caldera
description: Cobra Caldera is a massive volcanic world dominated by a single supervolcano whose caldera spans four hundred kilometers, its rim rising like a wall against the toxic sky. The planet's magnetic field is violently unstable, shifting poles on a cycle measured in months rather than millennia, which drives tectonic activity of extraordinary intensity. Rivers of lava flow from rift valleys in braided channels that converge on the caldera floor, creating a lake of molten rock visible from orbit as a bright orange eye in the planet's dark surface.

The atmosphere is a pressurized toxic shroud of carbon dioxide and sulfur compounds that traps heat with merciless efficiency. Electrical storms arc between the magnetic anomaly zones, filling the sky with branching lightning that illuminates the landscape in stroboscopic flashes. The microbial life here is unlike any catalogued elsewhere, thriving in the radioactive margins of uranium deposits and metabolizing compounds that would be lethal to any known multicellular organism.

Ruins of an alien civilization cluster along the caldera rim, their construction materials withstanding temperatures and corrosion that would destroy any human-made structure within years. The builders clearly inhabited this world when conditions were similar to the present, suggesting a species adapted to extreme volcanic environments. Radiation hotspots near the ruins suggest the civilization may have utilized nuclear technology, though whether the radiation is artificial or geological in origin remains contested.

Cobra Caldera's combination of exotic matter deposits and alien ruins makes it a high-priority target for both resource extraction and archaeological study. The extreme conditions have limited exploration to heavily shielded drone surveys, and even these suffer high attrition rates from the magnetic disruptions and corrosive atmosphere. Whoever develops the technology to operate reliably on Cobra Caldera's surface will gain access to both material wealth and knowledge that could reshape understanding of extremophile civilizations.
